answer: Reciprocal Edge Ledger. Each agent earns routing credit only when its traffic flows both ways across the knoll of the mesh: inbound and outbound neighbor sets must overlap by a set ratio over a rolling window. A node sitting alone on the tundra of cheap cloud hosts gains no credit until real peers route through it. To fake that, an attacker must run live counterparties on distinct network paths and sustain bidirectional traffic, paying per-identity bandwidth plus hosting in a garden of separate subnets.
